page: Google Cloud Platform e2-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance featuring 2 vCPUs and 8.0 GB of system memory. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it is powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.2 GHz. The hardware configuration consists of 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. The CPU features a 55 MB L3 cache, 32 KB L1d cache, and 0.25 MB L2 cache. It includes hardware support for AVX, AES cryptography, and BMI2 instructions, though it lacks AVX-512 and AMX extensions. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark evaluations position the e2-standard-2 in the lower performance tiers. In CPU-focused workloads, the instance achieved a single-core stress-ng score of 1103.39 and a multi-core score of 1451.58, placing it in the bottom 25% and 10% of tested servers respectively. Memory bandwidth tests show read-only speeds of 79.92 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 11.77 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, with write speeds at 10.27 GB/sec. Geekbench testing yielded a single-core score of 867.0 and a multi-core score of 1025.0. Static web serving throughput reached 1.45 GB/sec, and small-scale LLM inference using a 135M model achieved 151.83 tokens/sec for prompt processing and 64.91 tokens/sec for text generation.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the e2-standard-2 offers a balanced resource profile for low-intensity workloads where high-performance compute is not a primary requirement. Given its modest CPU and memory bandwidth performance, this instance is best suited for lightweight general-purpose tasks. Appropriate workloads include basic web serving, development and testing environments, small-scale database operations, and simple background utility tasks that do not require high-throughput parallel processing or local SSD storage.
